## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

On credential-withheld triggers, the Action can now retain static, credential-free local MCP servers instead of removing the entire `mcp` configuration. It drops remote servers, malformed entries, and definitions containing `{file:}` or `{env:}` references—even when those appear in nested or otherwise unknown fields—and removes `mcp` when nothing safe remains. Kept servers still run as operator code, so their commands and literal environment values are not sandboxed; fork pull requests remain subject to the caller's restrictions. [#2104](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2104)

The V1 harness is rebased onto upstream OpenCode 1.19.5, with the SDK, compatibility cap, and harness version references updated to match. After that harness build was published, the integration agent and workspace image defaults were moved to its `1.19.5+harness.bf7f7dfe` build; the production workspace image continues to override the V1 default with its V2 build. [#2097](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2097) [#2100](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2100)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Systematic now has a repository-level configuration that points past-work searches to the project’s RFCs, decisions, and wiki. The initial config’s trailing commas prevented the plugin from loading, so the file is now kept compatible with Systematic’s parser; CI path filters also ensure JSONC, root config, and lockfile changes trigger lint, build, and self-review checks. [#2086](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2086) [#2087](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2087) [#2088](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2088)

OpenCode V2 workspace images no longer leave provider credentials in a plaintext `auth.json` readable by tool processes. Startup removes any stale file (including a symlink, without following it), while V1 behavior remains unchanged; deployment documentation also clarifies that workspace users and bound repositories are trusted because tools run with access to the server’s credentials and data. [#2090](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2090)

The gateway’s Hono server dependency includes fixes for request-path and WebSocket edge cases with security implications. Raw backslashes in request paths are rejected, WebSocket upgrade URLs retain the `Host` header’s authority, and socket errors during asynchronous upgrades are handled instead of crashing the process. [#2074](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2074)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

You can now stop an active run from Discord with `/fro-bot cancel`, targeting it from the run thread or its bound channel. The command reports whether cancellation succeeded and posts a notice in the thread; it avoids cancelling quarantined runs, where owned work may still be running. [#2066](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2066) [#2063](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2063)

### Bug fixes

Gateway run ownership updates are now serialized and duplicate snapshots are skipped, preventing concurrent writes from losing to each other with a conditional-store conflict. The terminal write waits for pending ownership updates to drain, while retaining the existing stale-ETag retry as a backstop. [#2059](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2059)

Discord approval and question cards now show deciding actors where Discord renders them correctly: mentions appear in card descriptions instead of titles, and dashboard approvers appear as escaped plain-text logins rather than broken Discord mentions. Existing non-human decisions and mention suppression remain unchanged. [#2057](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2057) [#2061](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2061)

The Hono update includes fixes for middleware bypasses involving mounted paths and wildcard routes, skipped multipart form validation, CSS helper HTML injection, and CSRF checks for hyperlink-auditing requests. [#2062](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2062)

### Operations

The workspace shell-permission documentation now matches the gateway behavior: commands ask only when an operator rule matches, the last matching rule wins, and commands in compound expressions are checked individually. It also provides a working example for selectively prompting on commands such as `rm` and `sudo`. [#2064](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2064)

Renovate post-upgrade jobs now build only the committed Action bundle where needed, skip builds for lint-only and GitHub Actions updates, and avoid fetching the full AWS SDK changelog. This reduces work on update branches while retaining validation of the generated bundle and Renovate command configuration. [#2054](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2054)
